qualifying_findings.source_title: AI-Native Development Forces Teams To Define What Software May Change
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article page shows Sep 29, 2026 below the byline.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The article describes a practice model where agent-started work is gated before code is written: tickets are checked against current architectural decisions, CI rules block merge paths, and billing or pricing folders require human review. It also reports that high-level solution documents are maintained by agents and periodically read for code/documentation drift.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent throughput needs upstream work-in-progress limits and executable change boundaries, not only downstream review capacity. Architecture decisions, ticket baselining, protected paths, and drift checks become part of the agent operating model.

upstream_owned_entities.routing_note: Developer-tool background belongs upstream; local note should keep only protected-path and merge-gate practice implications.

qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Potential synthesis for pre-write ticket baselining, protected agent scopes, and architecture-decision checks. Treat interview claims as practitioner evidence.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Sonar Extends Agentic Code Governance and Verification to Self-Managed Infrastructure
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Press release header shows Sep 29, 2026, 11:30 ET.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Sonar announced SonarQube Server 2026.5 LTA with agentic capabilities for self-managed, on-premise, air-gapped, and VPC-restricted deployments. The release frames agentic code governance around context and constraints before writing, independent verification of changes, remediation controls, centralized LLM governance, MCP access, dependency risk checks, compliance reporting, and architecture visibility.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local practice signal is that agent governance is moving into sovereign infrastructure and layered verification: teams should separate context injection, independent verification, remediation automation, model/tool governance, and evidence generation when designing coding-agent controls.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Google Cloud MCP servers audit logging
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Documentation footer shows Last updated 2026-09-28 UTC.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Google Cloud documents audit logging for remote MCP servers, including service-name filtering, permission-type mapping to Data Access versus Admin Activity logs, and the fact that Data Access audit logs for MCP are disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled for DATA_READ.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: MCP access in coding-agent workflows needs explicit audit-log enablement and cost-aware logging decisions. A local governed-tool practice should distinguish administrative events from data access and record whether logs are actually enabled before relying on them as evidence.

upstream_owned_entities.routing_note: Cloud provider background belongs upstream; local note should keep only audit-log configuration and governed MCP practice implications.
Protocol background belongs upstream; local note should keep only auditability and permission practice implications.

qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Good candidate for a governed-MCP checklist: service filter, DATA_READ enablement, logging cost, and evidence retention.

qualifying_findings.source_title: OpenAI Codex Adds Cloud Environments, Voice CLI and Code Review
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The article reports Codex cloud environments, reusable team development environments with approved settings and permissions, CLI voice steering, multi-task delegation, session resuming, worktree integration, an app code-review surface, and the open-sourcing of the Codex harness. It recommends piloting shared environments, checking secrets management, and verifying session resume and worktrees before team rollout.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Reusable agent environments turn local sandbox setup into a shared governance artifact. Teams should test environment permissions, secrets exposure, review accountability, worktree isolation, and fallback paths before standardizing a cloud coding-agent workflow.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Is Claude API Build Eval Free
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article page shows Tuesday, September 29, 2026 and links the September 28 guide plus the September 29 public commit.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The article explains that Anthropic's build-eval and hillclimb workflows are public instructions, but running the generated evaluation can incur costs across Claude Code orchestration, the application under test, optional model judges, and retries. It cites a September 29 commit adding build-eval, eval-hillclimb, cost-hillclimb, eval-audit, report schema, report builder, and runner scaffold files to Anthropic's skills repository.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Eval automation needs an explicit spend model, not just a workflow. Local eval guidance should require cases, repetitions, variants, graders, retry rates, and hillclimb rounds to be budgeted before agentic optimization runs.

qualifying_findings.date_basis: Search result and page content show a Sep 28, 2026 update; page methodology describes the current scoring rubric.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Favur Evals publishes a multi-agent SDLC benchmark whose composite score weights per-agent roles toward code review and implementation, then planning and other roles. Its methodology combines artifact-quality scoring with efficiency metrics such as tokens, cost, error-cleanliness, static analysis, pytest results, deliverables manifests, and tool/transcript telemetry, while warning that scores are relative rankings under a versioned rubric.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local eval-practice implication is to score full delivery roles and telemetry, not only final pass/fail, and to pin historical results to rubric versions when the harness changes.

upstream_owned_entities.routing_note: Benchmark/product background belongs upstream if retained as an entity; local note should keep only role-weighted and rubric-versioned evaluation practice.

qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Before ingest, verify whether the page itself exposes the update timestamp sufficiently or use as lower-confidence practice evidence.

qualifying_findings.source_title: The code review gap I see in the AI-agent era
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Search result shows Published yesterday with Tuesday September 29, 2026; inspected page is publicly readable and shows relative timestamps.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The public discussion describes using a separate fresh-context review agent, requiring findings to reproduce or be dropped, fixing findings with failing tests, maintaining a short running note per feature, and distinguishing diff review from full-suite regression detection. Replies emphasize cold review by a different model, code maps or diagrams for intent, and reviewer independence from implementation context.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI code review practice needs evidence thresholds, fresh-context review, bounded review rounds, feature notes to avoid repeated false findings, and full-suite regression checks alongside diff-focused review.

upstream_owned_entities.routing_note: Product background belongs upstream; local note should keep only fresh-context review and evidence-threshold implications.
Product background belongs upstream; local note should keep only cross-agent review workflow implications.

qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Treat as practitioner discussion, not benchmark evidence. Useful for review-loop vocabulary after corroboration.
